title: Snake Bite? Ayurveda Says Bite Back!
description:
People often imagine Ayurveda as “all natural” and “herbal healing.” But what do the original Ayurvedic texts actually say? In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts exposes some bizarre passages from Susrutha Samhita and Caraka Samhita that are rarely spoken about.

For ascites (fluid-filled abdomen, often from liver cirrhosis), Susrutha recommends holding a patient upside down and shaking them until they vomit — or burying them in a heap of ash up to their neck.

For mental illness (unmaada), the texts prescribe crude and shocking remedies that have no medical basis.

For snake bites, Susrutha suggests you should literally bite the snake back. If that fails, bite a lump of clay, mix it with your saliva, and smear it on the wound. Alternatively, earwax will do.

These so-called “gems of Ayurveda” reveal the pseudoscience at the core of ancient practices. Real medicine comes from scientific testing, evidence, and progress — not ash baths, saliva smears, or snake biting.

If you’ve searched for “Ayurveda myths exposed,” “Susrutha Samhita snake bite cure,” “Caraka Samhita pseudoscience,” “Ayurveda bizarre treatments,” “Ayurveda debunked,” or “funny Ayurveda remedies”, this video uncovers the shocking truth behind ancient “gems.” Like, share, and subscribe for more myth-busting science content.
